And when Sergius entered first,
as Mu'awiyah had commanded,
then Andrew entered.
Sergius trembled, jumped up, and stood and did obeisance to Andrew.
Mu'awiyah, however, slapped Sergius,
meaning: "If this servant has terrified you so much,
had you seen his master,
how would you have been?" But Sergius replied:
"It was from habit that I was seduced and did this,
and not from fear."
Then Mu'awiyah asked Andrew:
"For what reason have you come?" And he replied:
"The emperor sent us so that the rebel might not deceive you.
For if towards his master and benefactor he has shown himself to be entirely such an evil recompenser,
how much more towards you?" But Mu'awiyah said:
"You are all our enemies,
and whoever increases the tribute to us,
him we help."
And Andrew replied:
"Even if it is so,
yet one enemy is superior to another enemy.
Neither are a slave and a master equal.
For a master comes forth to these matters with nobility and greater decorum,
whereas he who lives in slavish servility,
acts in a more slavish manner,
and as befits an abject person.
Therefore, what my master gives,
even if it should be less than what the rebel promises,
it is proper for you to trust him,
and not seek to bargain like a broker."
Andrew said these things and went out.
And on the next day Sergius came early.
And when Andrew came,
Sergius did not stand up for him.
And Andrew said to him:
"O despairing one,
why did you not stand up for me?" But he was insolent,
and insulted him as if he were an effeminate man.
And Andrew threatened Sergius that he would remove his testicles.
And Mu'awiyah said to Andrew:
"If you give us the tribute of your entire country,
let the name of the kingdom remain yours.
And if not,
depart."
Andrew, however, took courage and replied:
"Are the Arabs, then, possessed of bodies,
and the Romans shadows? Rather, we take refuge in God."
And he went out and made his journey via Melitene.
And he commanded the guards of the mountain passes (clisurae)
to seize Sergius as he passed by.
Now Mu'awiyah had promised Sergius to send an army; but when he returned, the men in ambush seized him
and brought him to Andrew.
And he commanded and they cut off his testicles and placed them in his hands,
and then he impaled him.
As for Sapor, before the army of the Arabs reached him,
he was crushed in the gate of his courtyard while riding, and died.
